primary_claim: Many GPT2 'glitch tokens' are BPE subtoken artifacts -- rare tokens that are substrings of much higher-frequency parent tokens (e.g. ' practition' vs ' practitioner'/' practitioners') -- and the numerical closeness of a subtoken's token-id to its parent token's id can be used to predict glitchiness and recover the token's likely training-data context without access to the model's training data.

effect.metric: token frequency of subtoken vs parent token in OpenWebText

contradicts_or_qualifies: qualifies the earlier hypothesis that glitch tokens were excluded from training data -- author argues this is unlikely to be true for most glitch tokens (to be elaborated in a follow-up post)
stated_future_work: explain why the hypothesis that many glitch tokens were excluded from training data is unlikely to be true for most glitch tokens
explore the role that glitch tokens play in improving LLM performance
limitations_stated: I'm not sure if this approach is useful for finding glitch tokens in other GPT models
